sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Cailitin is an Irish hero. He was a druid of the warrior class. The name also appears as Calatin or Calatín. One man and his twenty seven identical sons made up the figure. Each son lacked a left hand and a right foot. Cailitin learned sorcery in Scotland. He then served the great queen Medb. Medb set him against the hero Cúchulainn. Cúchulainn killed the whole force. The druid's wife then bore two sets of triplets. One set held daughters and one held sons. The daughters included the battle-crow Badb. Medb trained the women in wizardry. Their magic later brought about the death of the hero. The one-eyed daughters, with his rival Lugaidh mac, ended Cúchulainn.

okr.objective: Cailitin is a druid warrior whose kin helped end Cúchulainn.
